different types of high-fat diet differ in their effect in hepatic mitochondrial dynamics and morphology.

(a) a high-lard diet induces hepatic steatotic changes associated with mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress and mitochondrial fission; (b) high-fish-oils diets have an anti-steatosis and anti-oxidative effect associated with increased levels of proteins involved in fusion processes.

the role of mitochondria in the development of hepatic fat accumulation and insulin resistance in response to high-fat diets.
the effects of different types of high-fat feeding on mitochondrial function and dynamics.
the role of mitochondria in the development of hepatic fat accumulation and insulin resistance in rats fed high-lard and -fish-oil diets.

a high-lard diet, by inducing mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress, may be more harmful than a high-fish-oiland high-fat diet, as it may promote mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative damage, and thus may contribute to the development of insulin resistance and hepatic steatotic processes.
a diet high in saturated fatty acids induces a shift towards fission, whereas a diet rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids induces a switch towards fusion processes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a high-lard diet induces a mitochondrial dysfunction associated with a shift to a fission process.
high-lard feeding elicits mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress and mitochondrial fragmentation.

the high-lard diet, by increasing oxidative stress and shifting towards fission, may be involved in the pathogenesis of insulin resistance and hepatic steatogenesis, while the high-fish-oilediet, by reducing oxidative stress and stimulating fusion processes, may have an anti-steatogenic and anti-obesity action.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mitochondrial dysfunction present during the development of hepatic insulin resistance and steatosis is associated with a shift towards fission processes, whereas the use of a high-fat fish oil diet is able to prevent this shift.
the mitochondrial dynamics are affected differently by the type of high-fat diet, and that the type of fat in the diet may have important consequences on the metabolic effects of over-feeding.

the high-lard diet induces mitochondrial dysfunction associated with a shift towards fission processes, which is consistent with the hypothesis that this diet may contribute to obesity and hepatic steatotic disorders, and that fish oil may exert anti-steatotic and anti-obesity effects by favouring mitochondrial fusion processes.
